prompt:
Draw the land borders and coastline of Poland as of 1 January 1938 from memory.

Rules:
- Draw land only. Each separate piece of territory (mainland, island, exclave) is its own polygon. Do not enclose sea.
- Leave out overseas dependencies and Antarctic claims.
- Use at most 400 points in total.
- Your drawing is scored by overlap: the area it shares with the true territory, divided by the total area covered by either. Missing land and extra land both cost you.
- Give your best attempt even if you are unsure. An approximate drawing is expected.

Format:
- You may reason first. End with one ```geojson block; only that block is scored.
- The block holds a single GeoJSON MultiPolygon:
  {"type": "MultiPolygon", "coordinates": [[[[lon, lat], [lon, lat], ...]], [[[lon, lat], ...]]]}
- Longitude first, then latitude, in decimal degrees with at most 2 decimal places. West and south are negative.
raw:
I need to draw Poland's borders as of January 1, 1938. This is interwar Poland, which existed between WWI and WWII.

Key features of 1938 Poland:
- Western border with Germany (including East Prussia creating a discontinuity)
- Northern border along the Baltic Sea coast (including the "Polish Corridor" to Gdańsk/Danzig area)
- Eastern borders with Lithuania, Latvia (briefly), USSR (Belarus and Ukraine)
- Southern borders with Czechoslovakia and Romania
- Poland was larger in the east than modern Poland, extending further into what is now Belarus and Ukraine

Major cities to orient myself:
- Warsaw (roughly 21°E, 52°N) - central
- Kraków (20°E, 50°N) - south
- Lwów/Lviv (24°E, 50°N) - southeast (was Polish in 1938)
- Wilno/Vilnius (25.3°E, 54.7°N) - northeast (was Polish in 1938)
- Gdynia on Baltic coast (18.5°E, 54.5°N)

Approximate borders:
- Baltic coast: roughly from 14.5°E to 19°E around 54-55°N
- Western border: roughly 14-17°E going north-south
- Southern border: along Carpathians, roughly 49-50°N
- Eastern border: extended to about 26-27°E in places
